units.source_text: 著者在先，已写道“家将待着雨住”了。

en.t: The author has already written earlier that the servant was waiting for the rain to stop.

units.source_text: 然而这家将便在雨住之后，却也并没有怎么办的方法。

en.t: Yet even after the rain stopped, this servant still had no idea what he should do.

units.source_text: 若在平时，自然是回到主人的家里去。

en.t: In ordinary times, he would naturally have gone back to his master's house.

units.source_text: 但从这主人，已经在四五日之前将他遣散了。

en.t: But his master had dismissed him four or five days before.

units.source_text: 上文也说过，那时的京都是非常之衰微了；

en.t: As was said above, Kyoto at that time had fallen into extreme decline.

units.source_text: 现在这家将从那伺候多年的主人给他遣散，其实也只是这衰微的一个小小的余波。

en.t: The fact that this servant had now been dismissed by the master he had served for many years was really only a small ripple of that decline.

units.source_text: 所以与其说“家将待着雨住”，

en.t: So rather than saying that the servant was waiting for the rain to stop,

units.source_text: 还不如说“遇雨的家将，没有可去的地方，正在无法可想”，倒是惬当的。

en.t: it would be more accurate to say that the servant caught in the rain had nowhere to go and was at a loss for any solution.

units.source_text: 况且今日的天色，很影响到这平安朝家将的Sentimentalisme上去。

en.t: Moreover, today's weather had a strong effect on the Sentimentalisme of this Heian-period servant.

units.source_text: 从申末下开首的雨，到酉时还没有停止模样。

en.t: The rain that had begun toward the end of the Hour of the Monkey still showed no sign of stopping by the Hour of the Rooster.

units.source_text: 这时候，家将就首先想着那明天的活计怎么办——

en.t: At this moment, the servant first began thinking about what he would do for a living tomorrow.

units.source_text: 说起来，便是抱着对于没法办的事，要想怎么办的一种毫无把握的思想，

en.t: In other words, he was holding a completely uncertain thought, trying to decide what to do about something that could not be dealt with.

units.source_text: 一面又并不听而自听着那从先前便打着朱雀大路的雨声。

en.t: At the same time, without meaning to listen, he found himself hearing the rain that had long been beating down on Suzaku Avenue.
